title: BioIVT ETHNIC (Precision) and ETH (Detroit) use the shared canonical ETHNIC list, including Unknown
description: Points ETHNIC (Precision) and ETH (Detroit) at the shared canon_ethnic list: the 2 official CDISC ETHNIC (C66790) values plus Unknown, which Precision already collects but the official codelist does not formally allow (C66790 is non-extensible). Detroit gains an Unknown option it never had.
rationale: Dan's standing rule for BioIVT: CDASH wins on disagreement, but here the official codelist is non-extensible and applying it strictly would have dropped Precision's existing Unknown option. Explicit decision (2026-09-28): include Unknown anyway rather than lose it, understanding this is a deliberate deviation from strict CDISC compliance, not something the standard sanctions the way the CM-domain extensions (route/frequency/dose unit) were.
source: NCI EVS CDISC SDTM Controlled Terminology ETHNIC C66790; canonical-code-list-library plan step 1c

history.note: Unknown included by explicit decision despite the official codelist being non-extensible, to avoid losing an option Precision already collects. SEX/GENDER was the companion case and was resolved the opposite way (left uncanonicalized) since there was no clean way to add Other without contradicting the standard as clearly.
